answer: Before trading, each agent must forge a verifiable work history: it locks a refundable stake and completes small paid tasks under peer review. A trellis of reputation links every agent to the counterparties it served, so good work raises its score and proven fraud collapses it and slashes the stake. At dawn the network reweights scores by recent verified output, so a fresh identity starts at zero and cannot buy trust. Cloning identities multiplies the stake cost while trust stays near zero, so a Sybil farm pays far more than it can earn.
